title: OpenAI-compat: Responses v7 streaming fragment reassembly and metadata passthrough
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Responses v7 introduces non-deterministic chunking across numeric fragment IDs and expanded metadata fields. Customer integrations relying on deterministic streaming reassembly (toolcall frames, structured JSON outputs) are broken when fragments are split or merged by gateway layers. This PR implements a compatibility shim that (1) attaches compact sequence headers to streaming chunks, (2) reassembles fragments server-side for stable tool/function calling boundaries, and (3) forwards user-supplied metadata (X-RW-META-*) as passthrough attributes to the Redwood responses wrapper so downstream consumers see identical attributes to upstream OpenAI calls.

Summary of changes: added a fragment header protocol (x-rw-frag: <msg-id>/<seq>/<last-flag>), implemented a reassembly buffer in the openai-compat layer, preserved toolcall framing across chunk boundaries, and added a lightweight metadata proxy that copies prefixed headers into the responses metadata envelope. Also added a feature flag (openai_compat_v7_reassembly) and comprehensive e2e tests.

Design notes: the fragment header uses a 64-bit msg-id (hex), a monotonically increasing seq number per message, and a last-flag to mark final chunk. Reassembly is time-bounded (200ms default) and size-bounded (512KB) to avoid head-of-line blocking; these limits are configurable per-tenant. For tool/function calls we treat toolcall frames as atomic units during reassembly and we will not emit partial toolcall events. For structured output we add a validation pass to ensure top-level JSON objects are complete before forwarding.

Backward compatibility: when the feature flag is disabled the shim is inert (no headers added, no reassembly). The passthrough copies only headers matching the X-RW-META-* prefix to prevent header pollution. Existing SDKs are unaffected; however server-side consumers of streaming events should be updated to read x-rw-frag when consuming raw OpenAI-compatible streams.

Rollout: gated by feature flag and tenant opt-in. Will roll out to staging for 48h soak, then gradual canary across 5% of hosted traffic, then 25% and full roll by metric gates. Metrics to monitor: stream-reassembly-failure-rate, toolcall-split-detected, stream-latency-p50/p95, reassembly-buffer-fill, and memory-pressure-by-tenant.

Testing: unit tests for header parsing, reassembly timeout, toolcall frame boundaries; integration tests with python/ts SDK harness to verify toolcall event integrity; load test showing <2% p95 latency regression at 10k concurrent streams.

Related: Linear ENG-9921, ENG-10012, PM-204. Notes: does not change persisted model artifacts or KV cache behavior.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation 
- [x] Unit + integration tests 
- [x] Feature flag and config knobs 
- [x] Docs PR TBD (docs authored as follow-up)
- [x] Performance verification

If merged this resolves customer impact incidents SUP-88 and reduces flakiness observed in INT-417.

merge_commit_message:
compat(openai): v7 stream reassembly + metadata passthrough (feature-flagged)

Implements chunk headers, server-side reassembly, toolcall/frame preservation, and metadata proxying for X-RW-META-* headers. Includes tests and feature flag.
release_notes: Add server-side streaming fragment reassembly and metadata passthrough for OpenAI Responses v7 compatibility. Feature-flagged; opt-in per tenant. Improves streaming stability and preserves tool/function call integrity across chunk boundaries.
